verses.text: The LORD said to Moses,
"Speak to the people of Israel and tell them: A man or a woman may make a special promise to set himself apart for the LORD as a Nazirite.
Then he must stay away from wine and other strong drink. He must not drink vinegar made from wine or from other strong drink. He must not drink grape juice or eat grapes, fresh or dried.
As long as he is a Nazirite, he must not eat anything that comes from the grapevine, not even the seeds or the skins.
As long as his promise lasts, no razor may touch his head. Until the time he set apart for the LORD is over, he is holy, and he must let the hair of his head grow long.
As long as he is set apart for the LORD, he must not go near a dead body.
Even if his father, mother, brother, or sister dies, he must not make himself unclean for them, because the sign that he is set apart for God is on his head.
All the time he is a Nazirite, he is holy to the LORD.
If someone dies suddenly beside him and makes his long hair unclean, he must shave his head on the day he is made clean, the seventh day.
On the eighth day he must bring two doves or two young pigeons to the priest at the door of the Tent of Meeting.

The priest will offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, to make him right with God, because he sinned by being near the dead body. That same day he must make his head holy again.

He must set himself apart again for the LORD for the full time of his promise, and bring a one-year-old male lamb as a guilt offering. The days before do not count, because his time of being set apart was made unclean.
This is the teaching for the Nazirite when his time of being set apart is over: He must be brought to the door of the Tent of Meeting.

There he must bring his offerings to the LORD: a one-year-old male lamb with nothing wrong with it for a burnt offering, a one-year-old female lamb with nothing wrong with it for a sin offering, and a ram with nothing wrong with it for a peace offering.
He must also bring a basket of bread made without yeast: loaves of fine flour mixed with oil and thin wafers spread with oil, together with their grain offerings and drink offerings.
The priest will bring them before the LORD and offer the sin offering and the burnt offering.
He will offer the ram as a peace offering to the LORD, together with the basket of bread without yeast. The priest will also offer its grain offering and drink offering.
Then at the door of the Tent of Meeting, the Nazirite must shave off the long hair that showed he was set apart. He must take the hair and put it in the fire under the peace offering.
After the Nazirite has shaved off his hair, the priest will put in his hands the boiled shoulder of the ram, one loaf without yeast from the basket, and one wafer without yeast.

The priest will wave them in front of the LORD as a wave offering. They are holy and belong to the priest, together with the breast that was waved and the thigh that was given. After that, the Nazirite may drink wine.

This is the teaching for the Nazirite who makes a promise, and about the offering he must bring to the LORD for being set apart, besides anything else he can afford. He must do whatever he promised, following the teaching for the Nazirite."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Tell Aaron and his sons: This is how you must bless the people of Israel. Say to them:
'May the LORD bless you and keep you safe.
May the LORD smile on you and be kind to you.
May the LORD look on you with favour and give you peace.'
In this way they will put my name on the people of Israel, and I will bless them."
